<thought>All five candidate SMILES correspond to the molecular formula C₁₈H₂₁NO, which matches the mass‑spectrometric data. The ¹H NMR spectrum shows a 6 H singlet (consistent with an N,N‑dimethyl group), an aromatic region integrating to 8 H (two para‑disubstituted phenyl rings), a 2 H doublet around 4.5 ppm (a benzylic CH₂), and two additional methyl singlets. The structure that best fits these features is the compound containing an N,N‑dimethyl aniline linked to a second para‑substituted phenyl ring bearing a carbonyl‑ethyl substituent. Its SMILES string is:

**CCC1=CC=C(C=C1)N(C)C2=CC=C(C=C2)C(=O)CC**

This SMILES yields the correct formula and accounts for the observed NMR pattern, so it is the most plausible structure for the sample.</thought>
<final_answer>CCC1=CC=C(C=C1)N(C)C2=CC=C(C=C2)C(=O)CC</final_answer>
